node.title: Annex 2 — Plausibility and Technological Comparison
node.reading: This page is a technical verification annex to the public-facing foundation article . It is not the canonical source or a standalone article. For the authoritative technical material, use the canonical Ecosystem Positioning README and the versioned sources it indexes. This annex makes plausibility evidence and documentary technology walkthroughs inspectable and traceable. Publication on Tegrity.AI does not imply peer review, independent validation, production readiness, adoption as a standard or endorsement by the ITU, FG-TIDA or any cited organisation.
node.readingSummary: This page is a technical verification annex to the public-facing foundation article .

relations: The historical achievement and a present-day technology comparison require different baselines, evidence and claims.
Una reconstrucción documental no es un benchmark ejecutado ni permite declarar superioridad actual.
Documented provenance can establish what a comparison refers to without establishing that a comparative experiment has been executed.
Ni una tabla de productos ni una puerta de evidencia histórica constituyen por sí solas un experimento comparativo.
Positioning can compare problem classes, while any performance claim requires its own matched task, competent baseline and executed evidence.
El posicionamiento comercial no prueba un benchmark ni descarta capacidad de competidores no evaluada.
Adversarial regressions and a retained positive control support a bounded numerical claim, rather than a general certification of architectural effectiveness.
Se inspeccionaron código y pruebas fijados al commit; no se ejecutó una nueva campaña ni se convirtió CI en validación científica.
For a complementary reading, see [Claims, evidence and the limits of the comparison](https://tegrity.ai/when-the-controls-work-annex-9-claims-and-evidence-appendix/).
